_comment: What the USDA datasets we load do not hold, and how we work around it.
Started 2026-09-30 at the owner's word: 'start our own table of things that just
apparently aren't in USDA… add the specs for Maggi and everything else that we have
We load Foundation, SR Legacy and FNDDS (survey). Packaged products live in USDA's
Branded Foods dataset, which we do not load; when one exists, the entry cites it.
Like aliases.json this is our layer on top of usda.db, which is never edited.
An entry is reached from aliases.json by its id, which is NEGATIVE so it can never
be a USDA fdc_id. Ids are permanent: never reuse one.
kind 'food' — a food we specify: description, categoryId (a USDA category, so it
classes as USDA foods do), sodiumMgPer100g, portions, source, assumption.
kind 'form' — a form USDA lacks, counted as the USDA record `countAs` by dry matter:
both water figures read from usda.db at run time. Only a stated mass
converts. Every converted line says so (basis 'counted-as-dry').

maggi-seasoning.source: USDA FoodData Central, Branded Foods, fdc 2755366: MAGGI Seasoning, Nestlé, UPC 00028000111540 (the US 6.7 fl oz bottle), published 2026-03-12. Sodium 8,600 mg per 100 mL; label 430 mg per 1 tsp (5 mL), matching Nestlé Professional's label. Energy, fat and protein 0.
maggi-seasoning.assumption: Branded Foods gives liquids per 100 mL and Nestlé publishes no density, so Maggi takes soy sauce's (USDA 174277, Soy sauce made from soy and wheat: 1 cup = 255 g, 1.078 g/mL) and its portions. 8,600 mg / 1.078 = 7,979 mg per 100 g. Heuristics had matched 'Seasoning mix, dry, taco, original'.

fresh-wheat-noodles.description: Fresh wheat noodles, counted as dry pasta
fresh-wheat-noodles.note: The owner, 2026-09-30: fresh noodles are counted as dry noodles, with a note that we had to. USDA has no fresh wheat-noodle record; 'Pasta, fresh-refrigerated, plain, as purchased' (169727, 31.0% water) stands for the fresh form and 'Pasta, dry, enriched' (169736, 9.9%) for the dry, so a gram of fresh counts as 0.77 g of dry. Steamed, pre-cooked noodles hold more water than raw fresh ones, so for them the dry figure is an overstatement. See G22. Sodium follows the dry record (6 mg/100 g): ramen and chow mein noodles are salted in the dough, so their sodium reads low; before this, the fried chow mein match (866 mg/100 g) read far too high.

fresh-egg-noodles.description: Fresh egg noodles, counted as dry egg noodles
fresh-egg-noodles.note: As fresh-wheat-noodles, counted as 'Noodles, egg, dry, enriched' (169731, 9.0% water). USDA's only fresh pasta record (169727) stands for the fresh form. See G22.
